text:
acme_ops: Hey - we just onboarded Redwood Private and our users are getting kicked back at OAuth login when using Google sign-in. Error shows up as \"invalid_grant\" during token exchange. Happening for ~30% of attempts. We rolled back a config change but it keeps happening. Help?

Maya (Support): Sorry you're hitting this. Can you paste the exact error payload (from client) and confirm whether this is hosted or Private? Also which redirect URI is configured in the Google console?

acme_ops: This is Private (VPC). Redirect URI in Google console is https://auth.acme.example.com/callback (no trailing slash). Client getting response: {
  "error": "invalid_grant",
  "error_description": "Bad Request"
}

Maya (Support): Thanks. Can you also share the browser redirect URL (the one that contains the authorization code) and any client-side error logs? If you prefer, paste the full callback request headers (anonymize tokens).

acme_ops: Paste of the callback request path: /callback?code=4/ABCD123&state=xyz. The request to /oauth/token (server->google) returns 400 invalid_grant. No client-side errors other than the popup closing.

Maya (Support): Looping in Jia from Auth and Ethan from SRE. @Jia @Ethan - sounds like a token exchange failure with Google. Could be redirect_uri mismatch or PKCE code_verifier mismatch. Acme says redirect URI configured without trailing slash.

Jia (Auth): Thanks. acme_ops — can you run a quick capture of the token-exchange POST body (server side) and confirm the redirect_uri you send to Google's token endpoint? Also confirm whether you're including code_verifier for PKCE.

acme_ops: We send: grant_type=authorization_code&code=4/ABCD123&redirect_uri=https://auth.acme.example.com/callback/&client_id=redwood-client&code_verifier=xxxxx
  So we *are* sending a trailing slash in the POST (our server normalizes and appends /). Google console has the one without trailing slash.

Ethan (SRE): That mismatch can cause invalid_grant. Google requires exact match for redirect_uri in token exchange. The trailing slash difference explains the ~30% rate if some requests are normalized differently (e.g., some browser flows vs mobile). Repro steps we can use: 1) reproduce with curl to token endpoint while toggling redirect_uri. 2) check our auth proxy logs for normalization behavior.

DeployBot: New incident created: INC-2026-3542 (severity: P2) — assignees: Jia, Ethan.

Jia (Auth): I pulled the auth-proxy logs. There's a normalization layer that appends a trailing slash for requests routed through the envoy sidecar when X-Forwarded-Proto is set. Private deploys where customers front with their own LB sometimes hit a different code path and end up sending a different redirect_uri between initial auth redirect and token exchange. That's the race.

Maya (Support): Proposed immediate workaround for Acme: update the Google OAuth client to include both redirect URIs (with and without trailing slash) if allowed, or temporarily change the server to not append slash. Which is faster?

acme_ops: We can add the variant in Google console quickly. We'll do that now and report back.

acme_ops: Confirmed — adding the callback with trailing slash fixed the flow for our users. Thanks. But we want this fixed on your side so we don't have to manage duplicates.

Jia (Auth): Agreed. Action plan: 1) patch auth-proxy to canonicalize redirect_uri consistently (strip trailing slash during token exchange) and add a unit/e2e test for redirect normalization (PR target: eng-auth, branch: fix/oauth-redirect-normalize). 2) Add telemetry to detect redirect_uri mismatches and emit a clear error in logs (currently it's just invalid_grant). 3) Docs update: Console should display the exact expected callback URI including trailing slash note for Private.

Ethan (SRE): ETA: I'll ship the patch to staging today, run canary in Private envs. If all green, we'll release to production tomorrow. I'll also add a short runbook for support on how to triage redirect_uri mismatches (incl. curl snippet).

Maya (Support): Putting this as P1 for customer impact until fix is in prod. @Jia @Ethan please update the ticket with PR links. Acme, leaving this thread open — we'll follow-up when fix is deployed.

acme_ops: Thanks all. One additional oddity: some users also saw \"invalid_request\" with \"PKCE verification failed\" earlier today. Could be related.

Jia (Auth): Good catch. That can happen if code_verifier stored in session doesn't match due to state mismatch (some load balancers strip cookies). We'll review session affinity in the Private deploy path. For now, please ask users to retry if they get that — or we can temporarily disable strict PKCE check for that client (not ideal).

Ethan (SRE): Quick repro snippet for support runbook: ```bash
# simulate token exchange with mismatched redirect_uri
curl -X POST https://oauth2.googleapis.com/token \
  -d grant_type=authorization_code \
  -d code=4/FAKECODE \
  -d client_id=redwood-client \
  -d redirect_uri=\"https://auth.acme.example.com/callback/\" \
  -d code_verifier=xxxx
# Response: {"error":"invalid_grant","error_description":"Bad Request"}
```

DeployBot: Incident INC-2026-3542 updated: status=investigating, priority=P1.

Maya (Support): Thanks everyone. acme_ops — please let us know if you see any more cases after we finish the prod rollout. We'll follow up with PRs and release notes.

acme_ops: Will do. Appreciated!
